witness_description: The first witness in lexicographic order is (a,b,c,d)=(1,1,1,2). The four displayed statements have truth values (true,false,false,false).
refutation_explanation: For (a,b,c,d)=(1,1,1,2), (a-b)/(c-d)=0/(-1)=0 <= a/c=1, but c(a-b)=0 is not <= a(c-d)=-1; equivalently, b/d=1/2 is not >= a/c=1. Thus the first claimed equivalence fails because c-d is negative, so multiplying by c-d reverses the inequality.
search_space: All 256 ordered quadruples (a,b,c,d) in {1,2,3,4}^4 were visited in lexicographic order. The equivalence chain was evaluated exactly for all 192 quadruples with c!=d; the remaining 64 have an undefined first quotient because c=d.
